summary.text: Rick Jackson, a Republican and the founder of the health care staffing firm Jackson Healthcare, lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Georgia to Keisha Lance Bottoms.
He was a first-time candidate who spent more than $100 million of his own money in the primary campaign.

paragraphs.text: Jackson grew up in Atlanta, including in the Techwood Homes public housing community, and spent time in five foster homes.
He attended David Lipscomb College in Nashville but did not finish.
In 1976 he bought the staffing company where he worked and built it into Jackson Healthcare, an Alpharetta-based medical staffing firm that reports annual revenue above $3 billion.
He backed a 2022 Georgia law providing tax credits for donations supporting young people leaving foster care.
Jackson, a political newcomer, defeated Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in the June 16 Republican runoff.
He is married to Melody Moore Jackson, a Georgia Tech professor.
During the campaign, he proposed cutting the state income tax in half within four years, limiting property-tax increases, and expanding support for sheriffs and law enforcement.
He received 45.7% of the vote to Keisha Lance Bottoms's 54.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
